overview: Error wrapping lets one error embed another so you can add context as it travels up the stack while preserving the original cause for inspection.
`fmt.Errorf` with the `%w` verb wraps an error; `errors.Is` checks whether any error in the chain matches a sentinel; `errors.As` extracts a specific error type from the chain.
This replaced brittle string matching (strings.Contains(err.Error(), ...)) with structured, type-safe error inspection introduced in Go 1.13.
learningObjectives: Wrap errors with fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err) to add context while keeping the cause.
Compare against sentinel errors with errors.Is instead of == on a possibly-wrapped error.
Extract typed errors from a chain with errors.As to read their fields.
Decide when to wrap (add context) versus when to annotate without exposing internals, and implement Unwrap/Is/As on custom errors.
coreConcept.formalDefinition: Error wrapping is embedding a cause error inside another error that implements Unwrap() error; errors.Is walks the Unwrap chain testing equality (or a custom Is); errors.As walks it assigning the first matching concrete/interface type to a target pointer.
coreConcept.simpleExplanation: Wrapping is like putting a note on a problem before passing it up: 'failed to load user: <original error>.' The original is still inside, so higher-level code can ask 'is this ultimately a not-found error?' (errors.Is) or 'is there a database error in here I can read details from?' (errors.As) without parsing strings.
coreConcept.historicalContext: Before Go 1.13, libraries like github.com/pkg/errors popularized wrapping with stack traces and Cause(). Go 1.13 standardized the concept into the language's errors/fmt packages with the %w verb, Unwrap, errors.Is, and errors.As, making wrapping idiomatic and interoperable. Go 1.20 added wrapping of multiple errors with errors.Join and multiple %w verbs.

whyItMatters.business: Precise error classification lets services return correct status codes and retry only retryable failures, improving user experience and reliability.
whyItMatters.engineering: Structured errors replace fragile string matching, so refactors don't silently break error handling.
whyItMatters.scalability: Distinguishing retryable from terminal errors prevents retry storms that amplify load during incidents.
whyItMatters.cost: Better error context shortens debugging and incident time, cutting engineering cost.
whyItMatters.reliability: Preserving the cause while adding context yields accurate diagnostics and correct branching, reducing mishandled failures.

coreComponents.name: %w verb
coreComponents.definition: fmt.Errorf format verb that wraps an error.
coreComponents.purpose: Add context while keeping the cause inspectable.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Produce an error whose Unwrap() returns the wrapped error.

coreComponents.name: errors.Is
coreComponents.definition: Reports whether any error in the chain matches a target (sentinel).
coreComponents.purpose: Test for a known error value through wrapping.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Walk Unwrap, comparing == or calling Is(target).

coreComponents.name: errors.As
coreComponents.definition: Finds the first error in the chain assignable to a target type.
coreComponents.purpose: Extract a typed error to read its fields.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Walk Unwrap, assigning to the target pointer.

coreComponents.name: Unwrap()
coreComponents.definition: Method returning the next error in the chain.
coreComponents.responsibilities: Return the wrapped error (or nil at the end).

internalWorking: fmt.Errorf with %w returns a *fmt.wrapError that stores the message and the wrapped error and implements Unwrap() returning that error.
errors.Is(err, target) loops: it compares err == target, and if err has an Is(error) bool method it calls that; then it calls Unwrap and repeats until a match or the chain ends.
errors.As(err, &target) loops similarly: at each link it checks if the error is assignable to *target's type (or has an As method), assigns it, and returns true on the first match.
A single %w produces a linear chain; Go 1.20's errors.Join and multiple %w verbs produce a tree (Unwrap() []error), and errors.Is/As traverse the whole tree.
Sentinel errors are package-level values (var ErrNotFound = errors.New("not found")) compared by identity, which is why errors.Is must be used once they may be wrapped.
Custom errors can implement Is(target) error and As(any) bool to define matching semantics beyond plain equality (e.g., matching by code).
coreConcept.architectureFlow: low-level err -> fmt.Errorf("ctx: %w", err) -> higher wrap -> ... -> top handler: errors.Is(err, Sentinel)? branch ; errors.As(err, &typed)? read fields -> map to status/retry decision
dataFlowWalkthrough: The service wraps it: fmt.Errorf("get user %d: %w", id, err), adding context.
The handler wraps again or passes it up.
The top-level handler calls errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) to detect not-found and return 404.
Or it calls errors.As(err, &myDBErr) to read a structured DB error's code for finer handling.

keyTerminology.meaning: A predefined error value (e.g., io.EOF) compared by identity.
keyTerminology.importance: Use errors.Is to match it through wrapping.

keyTerminology.meaning: The sequence of errors linked by Unwrap.
%w wraps (keeps cause inspectable); %v only formats the text.
keyTerminology.importance: Only %w lets Is/As see the cause.
Creates a tree that Is/As traverse.

importantConcepts.explanation: fmt.Errorf with %v turns the cause into a plain string, severing the chain so errors.Is/As can no longer find it. Use %w when you want the cause inspectable; use %v when deliberately hiding it.

importantConcepts.concept: errors.Is for values, errors.As for types
importantConcepts.explanation: Use errors.Is to compare against a sentinel value; use errors.As to extract a concrete or interface error type so you can read its fields. They answer different questions.

importantConcepts.concept: Wrap to add context, but don't leak internals across boundaries
importantConcepts.explanation: Wrapping is great inside a package, but at an API boundary you may want to translate to a domain error (and decide whether to still wrap the internal cause) so callers don't depend on your implementation details.

variationsAndTypes: Custom errors implementing Unwrap/Is/As for custom matching.
advantages: Preserves the original cause while adding human context.
Type- and value-safe inspection (no string matching).
Composes across packages via the standard interfaces.
Enables precise retry/status decisions based on the real cause.
disadvantages: Over-wrapping produces long, noisy error messages.
Wrapping leaks implementation details if done across API boundaries carelessly.
Standard %w does not capture stack traces (need a library for that).

tradeOffs.whenToUse: Wrap when adding context that aids debugging and the caller may want to inspect the cause (errors.Is/As).
tradeOffs.whenToAvoid: Don't wrap when you intend to hide internals at a boundary, or when adding context adds no value (avoid redundant 'failed to: failed to:' chains).

coreConcept.realWorldAnalogy: Error wrapping is like a shipping label on a package as it moves through depots: each depot adds a sticker ('delayed at hub B: <previous label>') without removing the original contents. At the destination you can read every sticker (the chain) and still open the box to find the original item (errors.As) or ask 'did this ever pass through hub B?' (errors.Is).

commonMisconceptions.myth: You can compare wrapped errors with ==.
commonMisconceptions.reality: == only matches the outermost error; use errors.Is to match anywhere in the chain.
%v severs the chain (text only); only %w preserves the cause for Is/As.

commonMisconceptions.myth: errors.As just checks the type like a type assertion.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It walks the whole chain and assigns the first matching error to your target pointer.

productionConsiderations.scalability: Classify errors as retryable vs terminal via errors.Is/As so clients retry only safe failures and avoid retry storms during incidents.
productionConsiderations.reliability: Preserve the cause with %w so logs and metrics reflect the true root cause, improving incident accuracy.
productionConsiderations.faultTolerance: Map specific wrapped causes (timeouts, not-found) to the right fallback or status code.
productionConsiderations.monitoring: Aggregate errors by their root sentinel/type (via Is/As) rather than by message string for stable dashboards.
productionConsiderations.security: At API boundaries, translate internal errors to safe domain errors so you don't leak internals (file paths, SQL) to clients.
productionConsiderations.costOptimization: Accurate error classification shortens debugging, cutting incident and on-call cost.
productionConsiderations.performance: errors.Is/As walk the chain (O(depth)); keep chains reasonably shallow on hot paths.

codeExamples.title: Wrapping with %w and matching with errors.Is
codeExamples.overview: Wrap a sentinel error through layers and still detect it at the top.
codeExamples.breakdown: findUser returns the sentinel ErrNotFound; getUser wraps it with %w, adding context. At the top, `err == ErrNotFound` is false because err is the wrapper, but errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) returns true by walking the Unwrap chain. This is exactly why errors.Is replaces == once errors may be wrapped.
codeExamples.expectedOutput:
error: getUser 42: not found
matched ErrNotFound -> return 404
direct ==: false
codeExamples.commonIssues: Using %v instead of %w severs the chain so errors.Is returns false; comparing with == on a wrapped error always fails.
codeExamples.optimizationTips: Define sentinels once at package scope and document which functions can return them so callers know what to check with errors.Is.

codeExamples.title: Extracting a typed error with errors.As and custom Unwrap
codeExamples.overview: Define a structured error, wrap it, and pull it back out to read its fields.
codeExamples.breakdown: QueryError implements Error() and Unwrap(); fmt.Errorf wraps it once more. errors.As(err, &qe) walks the chain, finds the *QueryError, and assigns it so we can read Code and Query. errors.Is(err, ErrConn) traverses both wrappers (the fmt wrapper and QueryError.Unwrap) to find the root sentinel, letting us mark the failure retryable. This combines value matching (Is) and type extraction (As) on one chain.
codeExamples.expectedOutput:
got QueryError code=503 query=SELECT 1
root cause is a connection error -> retryable
codeExamples.commonIssues: Passing a non-pointer or wrong-typed target to errors.As panics or fails to match; forgetting Unwrap means Is/As can't see the inner cause.
codeExamples.optimizationTips: Implement a custom Is method on QueryError if you want matching by code rather than by the wrapped value.

endToEndExample.businessProblem: An HTTP API must return 404 for not-found, 503 with a retry hint for transient downstream failures, and 500 otherwise — all while logging the full root cause for debugging.
endToEndExample.inputData: Repository errors (sql.ErrNoRows, connection errors) that bubble up through service and handler layers.
endToEndExample.architecture: Each layer wraps errors with %w to add context; the handler inspects the chain with errors.Is and errors.As to choose the status code.
processingSteps: Service wraps with context: fmt.Errorf("loadOrder %d: %w", id, err).
Handler calls errors.Is(err, ErrNoRows) -> 404, and errors.As(err, &qe) to read a retryable code -> 503.
Everything else maps to 500; the full wrapped error is logged.
endToEndExample.output: Correct HTTP status codes driven by the true cause, plus a log line with the full error chain.
endToEndExample.monitoring: Group errors by root sentinel/type (via Is/As), not message string, for stable error-rate dashboards.
endToEndExample.errorHandling: Transient causes are classified retryable so the client/middleware retries only those; terminal causes are not retried.
endToEndExample.finalResult: Accurate, stable error classification and rich debugging context without fragile string matching.

industryUseCases.benefits: Uniform, type-safe error handling across the ecosystem.

industryUseCases.problem: Distinguishing retryable from terminal API errors.
industryUseCases.solution: Typed API errors inspected with errors.As/Is to drive requeue decisions.
industryUseCases.benefits: Controllers retry only what's safe, avoiding hot loops.

industryUseCases.problem: Mapping internal failures to safe client error codes.
industryUseCases.solution: Wrap internal causes, translate to domain errors at the boundary, classify with Is/As.
industryUseCases.benefits: Precise client responses without leaking internals.

productionDeepDive.scalability: Classifying errors as retryable vs terminal via errors.Is/As prevents retry storms that would amplify load during partial outages.
productionDeepDive.faultTolerance: Mapping specific wrapped causes (timeouts, connection errors) to fallbacks keeps the system degrading gracefully instead of failing hard.
productionDeepDive.highAvailability: Accurate transient-error detection lets clients retry safely, smoothing over brief dependency blips.
productionDeepDive.disasterRecovery: Preserved root causes in logs speed root-cause analysis and recovery after incidents.
productionDeepDive.performanceOptimization: Keep error chains shallow on hot paths since errors.Is/As traverse them; avoid wrapping in tight inner loops where context adds nothing.
productionDeepDive.costOptimization: Rich, structured error context reduces time-to-diagnosis, lowering incident and on-call cost.
productionDeepDive.securityConsiderations: At API/RPC boundaries, translate internal errors to safe domain errors so file paths, SQL, or stack details don't leak to clients.
productionDeepDive.monitoringAndObservability: Aggregate metrics by root sentinel/type rather than message string so dashboards stay stable as messages change.
productionDeepDive.dataQualityValidation: Use errors.As to read structured validation errors (field, reason) and surface precise, actionable messages.
productionDeepDive.loggingAndAlerting: Log the full wrapped chain at the top boundary once; alert on rates of specific root causes detected via errors.Is.

recommendedPractices: Wrap with fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err) when the caller may need to inspect the cause.
Use errors.Is for sentinel values and errors.As for typed errors instead of == or string matching.
Define sentinel errors once at package scope (var ErrX = errors.New(...)).
Implement Unwrap() on custom error types so Is/As can traverse them.
engineeringStandards: Never use strings.Contains on err.Error() for control flow.
Use %w (not %v) when you intend the cause to remain inspectable.
Translate internal errors to domain errors at public boundaries.
designRecommendations: Add context at each layer, but avoid redundant or noisy double-wrapping.
Decide deliberately whether a boundary should expose or hide the wrapped cause.
namingConventions: Name sentinels with the Err prefix (ErrNotFound, ErrTimeout).
Name custom error types with an Error suffix (ValidationError).
documentationStandards: Document which sentinel/typed errors each function may return.
Note whether a function wraps (preserves) or translates (hides) underlying errors.
testingStrategies: Assert error classification with errors.Is/As in tests, not string equality.
Test that wrapping preserves the cause through every layer.
Test custom Is/As/Unwrap implementations for correct matching.

commonMistakes.impact: The chain is severed; errors.Is/As can't find the cause.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Use %w to wrap when the cause must stay inspectable.

commonMistakes.impact: Match fails because the outer wrapper != sentinel.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Use errors.Is(err, sentinel) to match anywhere in the chain.

commonMistakes.impact: Fragile; breaks when messages change and across languages.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Use sentinels with errors.Is or typed errors with errors.As.

commonMistakes.mistake: Passing a non-pointer target to errors.As.
commonMistakes.impact: Panic: target must be a non-nil pointer to an error type.
commonMistakes.correctApproach: Pass the address of a variable of the target error type (e.g., &perr).

comparisonSection.explanation: Is answers 'is this that specific error?'; As answers 'is there an error of this type to read fields from?'
Only %w keeps the cause inspectable by Is/As; %v deliberately hides it.
Structured inspection is type-safe and refactor-proof, unlike fragile string matching.

beginnerQuestions.question: What does the %w verb do in fmt.Errorf?
beginnerQuestions.answer: It wraps the given error so the returned error's Unwrap() yields it, keeping the cause inspectable by errors.Is/As.

beginnerQuestions.question: When do you use errors.Is versus errors.As?
beginnerQuestions.answer: errors.Is matches against a sentinel value; errors.As extracts a specific error type so you can read its fields.
beginnerQuestions.explanation: Checks understanding of the two inspection APIs.

intermediateQuestions.question: Why can't you compare a wrapped error with == to a sentinel?
intermediateQuestions.answer: Because the wrapper is a different value than the sentinel; you must use errors.Is, which walks the Unwrap chain.
intermediateQuestions.explanation: Tests understanding of wrapping vs identity.

intermediateQuestions.question: What's the difference between %w and %v in fmt.Errorf?
intermediateQuestions.answer: %w wraps the error (Unwrap returns it; Is/As can find it); %v only formats its text, severing the chain.
intermediateQuestions.explanation: Tests a subtle but critical distinction.

advancedQuestions.question: How do errors.Is and errors.As traverse a chain, and how do custom Is/As methods change behavior?
advancedQuestions.answer: They loop calling Unwrap; Is compares == or calls a custom Is(target) bool, As checks assignability or calls a custom As(any) bool. Custom methods let you match by code or adapt types beyond plain equality.
advancedQuestions.explanation: Tests deep knowledge of the matching algorithm and extensibility.

advancedQuestions.question: What does errors.Join enable (Go 1.20+)?
advancedQuestions.answer: It combines multiple errors into one whose Unwrap returns []error, forming a tree that errors.Is/As traverse; fmt.Errorf also supports multiple %w verbs.
advancedQuestions.explanation: Tests up-to-date knowledge of multi-error support.

scenarioBasedQuestions.scenario: After a refactor, the API started returning 500 for not-found cases that used to return 404.
scenarioBasedQuestions.thinkingProcess: Likely the handler compared with == or string-matched, and a new wrapping layer broke it.
scenarioBasedQuestions.expectedAnswer: Replace == / string matching with errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) (and errors.As for typed errors), and ensure every layer wraps with %w so the sentinel remains findable.

systemDesignQuestions.problemStatement: Design an error-handling strategy for a multi-layer service that needs precise status codes, retry decisions, and safe client messages.
systemDesignQuestions.designApproach: Define sentinels and typed errors at the repo layer, wrap with %w through services, inspect with errors.Is/As at the handler to set status/retry, and translate to safe domain errors at the public boundary.
systemDesignQuestions.tradeOffs: Wrapping preserves debugging context but risks leaking internals if not translated at boundaries; deeper chains cost O(depth) to inspect.
systemDesignQuestions.scalingStrategy: Classify retryable vs terminal centrally so middleware retries only safe errors, preventing retry storms; aggregate metrics by root cause type.

keyConcepts: errors.As(err, &typed) to extract a type and read fields.
Implement Unwrap() on custom errors so Is/As traverse them.

go test ./...  # assert with errors.Is/As, not strings
interviewPoints: == fails on wrapped errors; use errors.Is.

Define sentinels with the Err prefix at package scope.
Translate internal errors at public boundaries.

keyTakeaways: Wrap errors with fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err) to add context while keeping the original cause inspectable.
Use errors.Is to match sentinel values and errors.As to extract typed errors — never == or string matching on wrapped errors.
Implement Unwrap (and optionally custom Is/As) on custom error types so the standard helpers can traverse your chain.
Wrap to aid debugging and classification, but translate to safe domain errors at public boundaries and keep chains shallow on hot paths.
